target_constraint: Must minimize polyethylene wear under 10+ million flexion cycles
observed_phenomenon: Tibial insert wear causing implant loosening and pain
mechanism: Excessive posterior tibial slope causes flexion gap instability, which drives polyethylene wear and subsequent metallic debris release, leading to implant loosening and systemic toxicity.
intervention: Redesign the tibial insert and baseplate to incorporate a slope-limiting constraint (e.g., a built-in anterior wedge or adjustable locking mechanism) that prevents posterior tibial slope beyond a safe range during implantation, thereby reducing flexion gap instability and minimizing polyethylene wear under cyclic loading.
expected_effect: Reduced polyethylene wear and associated metallic debris release, lowering the risk of implant loosening and pain over 10+ million flexion cycles.
falsification_test: In a cadaveric or computational knee simulator, implant the modified tibial component with a posterior slope of 10° (exceeding the safe limit) and subject it to 10 million flexion cycles; if polyethylene wear volume or wear rate is not significantly lower than that of a standard highly cross-linked polyethylene insert under the same slope, the intervention fails.
source_spans: "excessive posterior tibial slope caused flexion gap instability and polyethylene wear with subsequent metallic debris release"
